decisions.quote: Messenger RNA levels of betatrophin were induced about fivefold as determined by quantitative RT-PCR ( Fig. 1 B ), similar to what was published previously for C57BL/6 mice ( 9 ). However, betatrophin mRNA levels were not increased in gonadal white adipose tissue after S961 treatment as had been reported by Yi et al. ( 9 ), possibly due to the different mouse strains used or fat depots analyzed ( Fig. 1 C ).
decisions.reason: The authors confirm Yi et al.'s findings of S961-induced hepatic betatrophin expression and dramatic mouse β-cell replication, while explicitly contrasting the lack of betatrophin mRNA induction in mouse white adipose tissue and finding no replication response in transplanted human β-cells. Because the close replication in mice succeeded on the primary hepatic and proliferation effects but failed on the contrasted adipose expression finding (and in the conceptual extension to human islets), the outcome is mixed rather than failed.
